For example, in a regression problem, I realized doing clustering and generating a new feature with clustered labels and then proceeding with regression helped me increase accuracy. And next, EDA is advanced version of reporting or similar thing to visualization. dashboard. Business wise, it adds or might add much more value than modelling. If your model fails, your client may still be happy with insights you gave from EDA. Hence, it's a selling point as well. May be backup deliverable. 
EDA is exhaustive, there are some basic factors to check but it's not a single point where you stop. If you are keen on getting good at EDA, go to kaggle, pick most popular competitions and check out all kernels with EDA in title. If you are keen on hands on, focus on coding as well.
